newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were at a standstill with no reported trades, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light at $67.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00.

Sales were not expected until Wednesday amid ideas that packers were comfortably supplied with live cattle inventories following last week's active trading, which cleaned up most feedlot showlists, they said.
Fed cattle prices were expected to remain unchanged from sales late last week at $68.00, the sources said.
Light declines in beef prices Friday and Monday spurred ideas that prices had peaked, which could limit attempts to sell fed cattle at higher prices, they said.
Beef prices Monday were quoted down $0.20 to up $0.14 per cwt, with 179 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.

Showlists this week were estimated near 99,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, up 1,000 from last week, market sources said. The Kansas showlist was pegged near 88,000 head, down 1,900 from last week, they said.
Nebraska's showlist was estimated near 80,000 head, up 4,000 from last week.
